correctness.rationale: For any finite commutative local R with m^3=0 and dim_k(m^2)=1, multiplication gives a nonzero k-bilinear symmetric B on V=m/m^2 even in mixed characteristic. Its radical preimage is Soc(R). For non-socle a the annihilator is the inverse image of the hyperplane ker B(a,-); equality of these hyperplanes is equivalent to the same projective line in V/rad(B), and distinct ones are incomparable. Counts (q^{r+1}-1) socle elements and q^{r+1}(q-1) elements per projective line yield the claimed clique join. Universal vertices and clique components reconstruct q,r,t in the noncomplete case. The two ternary rings are separated by existence of a nonsocle square-zero element. A standalone exact program computes all annihilators and edges in eleven finite ring instances, including nonsplit characteristics; finite checks supplement, not replace, this proof.

value.rationale: Determines the entire new annihilator-inclusion graph for a broad natural class of finite local rings, including degenerate pairings and mixed-characteristic examples. It computes clique and chromatic numbers in response to a direction explicitly suggested in the originating 2026 article, characterizes which graph invariants recover residue-field and multiplication-rank data, and supplies nonisomorphic local algebras with the same graph. This is not a renamed graph invariant or an arbitrary finite sample.
